candidates.exact_span: The annual whole sludge application rate for the sewage sludge that does not cause any of the cumulative pollutant loading rates in Table 2 above to be exceeded, unless the pollutant concentrations in Table 3 found in Element I, Section III below are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether compliance is measured against the Table 2 cumulative loading-rate cap or the Table 3 concentration criteria changes which numeric limit applies (A), what pollutant data must be monitored or documented (B), and what evidence is expected when results are absent (C).

candidates.exact_span: If bulk sewage sludge is applied to land in a State other than the State in which the sludge is prepared, written notice shall be provided prior to the initial land application to the permitting authority for the State in which the bulk sewage sludge is proposed to be applied.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interstate land application triggers a pre-application written-notice obligation; whether that condition is met changes which notification requirements are applicable (B) and whether missing notice constitutes a documented no-obligation state or an unresolved evidence gap (C).

The enumerated notice contents that follow this lead-in define required notification elements; different readings of what must be included change evaluated monitoring/notification obligations (B) and whether absent items are non-required or missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall give 60 days prior notice to the Director of any change planned in the sewage sludge practice.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 60-day advance-notice requirement applies to planned practice changes; interpretation of what counts as a planned change or when the clock starts affects whether notification was required for a given period (B) and how to classify periods without notice records (C).

candidates.exact_span: Any change shall include any planned physical alterations or additions to the permitted treatment works, changes in the permittee's sludge use or disposal practice, and also alterations, additions, or deletions of disposal sites.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The scope of changes subject to prior notice determines whether a given facility event triggers the 60-day notification obligation (B) and whether lack of notice reflects no required change versus unresolved applicability (C).

candidates.exact_span: These changes may justify the application of permit conditions that are different from or absent in the existing permit, including notification of additional disposal sites not reported during the permit application process or absent in the existing permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If a practice change justifies new or different permit conditions, the operative numeric limits and site-specific requirements may shift from those in the existing permit, changing limit applicability (A), monitoring/notification duties (B), and how to treat evidence tied to superseded conditions (C).

candidates.exact_span: Change in the sludge use or disposal practice may because for modification of the permit in accordance with 40 CFR 122.62(a)(1).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a sludge use or disposal change is treated as cause for permit modification affects which permit terms—including limits and monitoring conditions—are in force during FY2025 (A/B) and whether obligations remain unresolved pending modification (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall provide the location of all existing sludge disposal/use sites to the State Historical Commission within 90 days of the effective date of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This imposes a time-bounded location-reporting obligation to the State Historical Commission; whether the 90-day window and effective-date trigger are satisfied changes evaluated reporting requirements (B) and the classification of missing location submissions (C).

candidates.exact_span: In addition, the permittee shall provide the location of any new disposal/use site to the State Historical Commission prior to use of the site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: New-site use is conditioned on prior location reporting; interpretation of when a site becomes a new disposal/use site and when use begins affects whether pre-use reporting was required (B) and how to treat periods before first use (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall within 30 days after notification by the State Historical Commission that a specific sludge disposal/use area will adversely affect a National Historic Site, cease use of such area.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A State Historical Commission adverse-effect notice can prohibit continued use of a site; whether that condition is met changes applicable discharge/application limits at the site (A), ongoing monitoring and use obligations (B), and whether absence of use reflects a documented prohibition versus unresolved status (C).

candidates.exact_span: The sludge documents will be retained on site at the same location as other NPDES records.
candidates.computation_change_reason: On-site retention at the NPDES records location defines where required sludge documentation must be kept, affecting whether recordkeeping obligations are met (B) and whether missing off-site evidence reflects non-compliance or an unresolved retrieval question (C).

candidates.exact_span: The person who prepares bulk sewage sludge or a sewage sludge material shall develop the following information and shall retain the information for five years.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The five-year development-and-retention duty sets who must create and preserve sludge records and for how long, changing evaluated recordkeeping obligations (B) and whether absent records fall inside or outside the required retention window (C).

candidates.exact_span: If the permittee supplies the sludge to another person who land applies the sludge, the permittee shall notify the land applier of the requirements for recordkeeping found in 40 CFR 503.17 for persons who land apply.
candidates.computation_change_reason: When sludge is supplied to a separate land applier, an additional notice obligation arises and recordkeeping responsibility may shift under 40 CFR 503.17; different readings of the supply/land-apply relationship change which party's monitoring and record obligations are evaluated (B) and where missing evidence should be attributed (C).

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 3 found in Element I, Section III and the applicable pollutant concentration criteria (mg/Kg), or the applicable cumulative pollutant loading rate and the applicable cumulative pollutant loading rate limit (kg/ha) listed in Table 2 above.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This clause requires retention of measured pollutant concentrations and the applicable Table 3 criteria or Table 2 cumulative loading values; interpretation of the 'or' alternative changes which numeric standards govern compliance comparisons (A), which parameters must be documented (B), and whether missing records indicate required-but-absent evidence versus a non-applicable pathway (C).
